**Account switching is feasible for both CLIs by selecting an account-specific directory when starting a new process.** The app does not currently do this: agent runs and usage polls inherit the same environment ([runner](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:153)).

| CLI | Credential storage | Save and restore |
|---|---|---|
| **Codex** | `CODEX_HOME/auth.json` when file storage is selected; otherwise the OS credential store or process memory. | **Yes for file storage.** OpenAI explicitly documents copying `auth.json` to restore a login. Set a different `CODEX_HOME` per account. A keyring login cannot be assumed to be copyable. [OpenAI authentication docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth) |
| **Claude Code** | On Windows, `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json`, or `.credentials.json` under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. | **Separate accounts are supported** by using a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` per account and logging in within each directory. Anthropic documents `/login` and `/logout` as managing the credential file; it does **not** document copying that file as a restore procedure, so that part needs a practical test. [Anthropic authentication docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication), [environment reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) |

Switching would need the selected environment applied consistently to runs, model discovery, and usage polling. Existing running CLI processes would retain their original account. Credentials are secrets, and expired or revoked logins may require signing in again.
> CODEX_HOME/

> CODEX\_HOME/

what is this folder in windows

`CODEX_HOME` is an environment variable pointing to Codex’s data folder. On Windows, its default is `C:\Users\<your-name>\.codex`—on your machine, `C:\Users\janbo\.codex`.

So `CODEX_HOME/auth.json` means `C:\Users\janbo\.codex\auth.json` **unless** `CODEX_HOME` has been set to another folder. Codex may use the Windows credential store instead of that file.

ok. lets think about an easy approach we can use that allows the user to follow a couple of steps to set up multiple accounts per agent.

things I am thinking of:

  * 'new': we start the agent and send the /login command. user must then specify username and pwd, when done, we copy the new credentials file
* we keep the list of credential files or we create config dirs per account
* we should be able to select the 'default account' and assign an account per action, similar like we do now already for agent, model,...

I’d use **one configuration directory per account**, rather than keeping copies of individual credential files. The CLI can then update its own credentials when tokens refresh.

A simple setup flow would be:

1. In agent settings, choose **Add account** and give it a name.
2. Choose **Use current login** (keep using the existing CLI configuration) or **Sign in to another account** (create a separate directory and launch that CLI’s login flow).
3. Choose a default account for each agent. Actions can override it with a specific account.

One correction to the proposed login step: MD² should never ask for a username or password. Codex uses `codex login`; Claude Code uses `/login`. The user completes authentication in the CLI and browser. Codex supports `CODEX_HOME`; Claude supports `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. [Official OpenAI documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth), [Claude Code documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication).

The main design decision is **conversation continuity**. Today provider sessions are associated with an agent, with no account recorded. I recommend pinning each conversation’s provider session to the account that created it; an action’s account choice would apply to a new conversation. That avoids attempting to resume a session under a different login. Model discovery and usage polling would also need to run under the selected account.

* 'add account' is ok, name can be deduced from folder name, but user can change it. 
* we always have the 'primary' account, which is the first account, currently used by the cli, name can be changed. but the idea is, if the cli is there and it already has account details, that is the initial one, then all other folders are the 'extra' accounts
* then we can indeed add a 'default' account to each agent. user can select accounts from the same menu as the agent, model,...

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

we update [usage\_metrics.csv](design/usage_metrics.csv) on a regular basis in the project. but it does not seem to use the [commit\_batcher.ts](app/src/data/commit_batcher.ts) for committing the file?

## Current state

* The desktop `UsageMetricsService` (`desktop/src/actions/agent/usage_metrics_service.js`) appends rows to `<projectFolder>/usage_metrics.csv`:
  * `token_usage` rows after each agent turn (`recordTokenUsage`, called from `agent_runner_service.js` and `agent_streaming_event_handlers.js`).
  * `account_usage` rows whenever the Claude or Codex rate-limit snapshot changes (`recordAccountUsage`). The Claude usage poll repeats every `AGENT_USAGE_POLL_TICK_MS` (2 minutes), so these rows are written even when no agent runs.
* After each append, `appendRecords` only calls `uncommittedProjectWrites.mark(rootPath, [filePath])`. Nothing notifies the renderer and nothing schedules a commit.
* `uncommittedProjectWrites.commit(rootPath)` runs only inside `integrateWorktree` and `continueMergeConflict` in `desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js`. Result: the file stays modified in the primary worktree until the next worktree integration. Projects that do not integrate worktrees never commit it.
* Other desktop-written files already reach Git differently:
  * activity files and the token usage summary are committed directly by the desktop (`commitTrackedPaths` in `project_agent_token_usage.js`);
  * conversation view state is committed through the renderer `CommitBatcher`: `agent_acknowledgement_service.ts` calls `DataService.scheduleRepositoryPathCommit(path, message)`, which queues a `kind: 'path'` change. At flush time, the desktop `commit` in `project_files.js` stages that path as it is on disk and commits it together with the rest of the batch. A path that no longer exists is skipped.
* There is no desktop-to-renderer event for usage metrics writes. Existing desktop-to-renderer subscriptions (for example `onActionConversationViewed`, `onClaudeRateLimits`) use `SUBSCRIPTION_METHODS` in `desktop/main.js`, `subscribeBridge` in `desktop/src/shell/preload.js`, and a handler in `local_bridge_dispatch.js`.

## Implementation details

Goal: every usage metrics append is committed through the shared `CommitBatcher`, using the same `kind: 'path'` mechanism as conversation view state. The batcher's delay (`AUTO_COMMIT_DELAY_MS`) groups frequent appends into one commit.

### Desktop

* `UsageMetricsService` extends `EventTarget`. After a successful `appendFile` in `appendRecords`, it dispatches a `written` event (`USAGE_METRICS_WRITTEN_EVENT`). The `CustomEvent` detail is `{ path }`: the repository-relative path of the CSV with forward slashes (for example `design/usage_metrics.csv`). No event is dispatched when the append fails or when `recordAccountUsage` finds no changed window.
* Keep `uncommittedProjectWrites.mark(...)`. It stays the fallback: if the renderer is not subscribed or scheduling fails, the next integration still commits the file. When the batcher already committed the file, `commitTrackedPaths` finds no staged changes and does nothing.
* `local_bridge_dispatch.js`: add `onUsageMetricsWritten(callback)` to `actionBridge`. It calls `addEventListener` on the injected `usageMetricsService`, forwards `event.detail` to the callback, and returns a cleanup that calls `removeEventListener`. Pass `usageMetricsService` into `createLocalBridgeDispatch` from `desktop/main.js`.
* `desktop/main.js`: add `'onUsageMetricsWritten'` to `SUBSCRIPTION_METHODS`.
* `desktop/src/shell/preload.js`: add `onUsageMetricsWritten: (callback) => subscribeBridge('onUsageMetricsWritten', [], callback)`.
* Remote control is not changed. The desktop window's renderer owns this commit.

### App

* `app/src/data/electron_action_bridge.ts`: add an optional `onUsageMetricsWritten?(callback: (event: UsageMetricsWrittenEvent) => void): () => void` with `UsageMetricsWrittenEvent = { path: string }`.

We need to add a new component to the run button on the card popups when an action is running on the card that has a task list.

With task lists, we can show a progress bar to show how far along the agent already is. A task list, is a list, it has multiple items, so we can turn that into a progress bar.

Use a horizontal progress bar, just below the run button.

We need to be careful when loading the component, it doesn't need to be there on every run button, only those that are currently running an action.

The component should be stand alone, so it monitors the changes, it is not provided with the progress value, but with the info needed to identify task list to track.

## Current state

* `CardRunButton` (`app/src/components/actions/run/trigger/card_run_button.tsx`) is rendered in each board card by `project_card_view.tsx`. It subscribes to the card context's first active run through `useRunningActionForContext`; that summary contains `runId` and status, but no task-list data.
* A live task list is stored at `ActionRun.conversation.taskList`. Each `agentTaskList` update replaces that list in `ActionRunRegistry`, and `useRunSelector(runId, selector)` provides a run-scoped subscription.
* `AgentTaskList` (`app/src/components/actions/conversation/tasks/agent_task_list.tsx`) already shows the same model in the action popup and defines progress as completed tasks divided by all tasks. Board cards currently show only the animated running border around the Run button.

## Implementation details

* Add a standalone `TaskProgressIndicator` component beside `CardRunButton`. It receives only `runId`, selects `run.conversation.taskList` with `useRunSelector`, and computes `completed / total` itself. Do not pass task data or a computed percentage from the parent.
* Render a determinate MUI `LinearProgress` directly below the Run button. style it only with theme values from `design/STYLE_GUIDE.md`.
* The completed and total counts are shown in a tooltip. the progress should not display any text directly, it should use the minimal amount of space possible.
* Return `null` when the selected run has no task list or an empty task list. Task additions, removals, and status changes update the bar through the run-store subscription.
* In `CardRunButton`, mount the indicator only when the live run status is exactly `running`, passing `runningRun.runId`. Keep showing it for queued, waiting-for-input but do not show when idle, or terminal state. 
* Keep current button state priority, tooltip, click behavior, and scheduled indicator unchanged.
* Wrap the button and indicator in a compact vertical layout so the bar sits below the button without changing other footer controls. No task model, action protocol, persistence, registry, or desktop changes are needed.
* Add focused React Testing Library coverage for the new component and its `CardRunButton` integration. Run affected tests and `npm run lint` in `app`.

## Acceptance criteria

* While a card action has status `running` and a non-empty task list, a horizontal progress bar appears directly below that card's Run button.
* Progress equals completed task count divided by total task count; pending and in-progress tasks are not counted as completed.
* Bar updates when the active run publishes a replacement task list, without reopening the card or action popup.
* No bar appears for a missing or empty task list, or while run is queued, waiting for input, idle, or finished.
* Concurrent cards read their own active run by `runId`; one card's task updates do not change another card's bar.
* Existing Run button states, popup opening, schedule marker, and card footer controls keep current behavior.
* Progress bar exposes determinate value and completed/total context to assistive technology, works in light and dark themes, and focused tests plus app lint pass.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

# App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

## 3. Layout

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.
- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required 
[3715 characters omitted]
’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.
- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.
- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.
- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.
- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).
- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.
- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.

---

## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)

- **Buttons:** `Button variant="contained"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant="outlined"` = secondary; `variant="text"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).
- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.
- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.
- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.
- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.
- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.
- **Select:** `size="small"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.
- **Menu / context menu:** all `Menu` / `MenuItem` dropdowns and right-click context menus are dense by default through the theme. Call sites must not set density; `Select` option lists inherit the same density.
- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.
- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). Bands separated by hairlines; footer on a `background.default` bar with top hairline; actions right-aligned (outlined Cancel + contained CTA). `autoFocus` first field; submit on `Enter` (`âŒ˜/Ctrl+Enter` in a textarea); close on `Esc`/backdrop â€” except that a dialog holding unsaved multi-field input may refuse `backdropClick` (return early from `onClose(event, reason)`) so a stray click on the scrim cannot discard typed values; `Esc` and the Cancel button must still close it, and Cancel stays visible and enabled, including while loading.
- **Empty state:** dashed target â€” `1.5px dashed custom.borderStrong`, radius 10, centered icon + `custom.text4` label. No "click to add" placeholder blocks.

---

## 9. Definition of done for a new component

1. Zero hardcoded hex / raw px colors â€” every value comes from `theme.palette` / `theme.shape` / `theme.spacing` / `theme.typography`.
2. Correct roleâ†’slot mapping (Â§2); at most one `primary` CTA on the surface.
3. Borders at rest, shadow only when floating (Â§5); bands split by a single hairline.
4. Hover **and** focus states on every interactive element (Â§7); icon buttons have tooltip + `aria-label`.
5. Body scrolls, header/footer pinned; `minWidth: 0` on flex children that hold long text.
6. Toggle to dark mode and confirm nothing breaks â€” if it does, you hardcoded a color somewhere (Â§1).

Component-specific detail lives in `GUIDANCE.md` (theme definition + board/list/dialog), `CARD_POPUP_GUIDE.md`, `RUN_DIALOG_GUIDE.md`, and `SIDEBAR_ACTIONS_GUIDE.md`.

Allow separate Codex and Claude accounts to be configured, selected as defaults, assigned to actions and runs, and remembered by provider sessions in a conversation.

this card was split up into the following sub sections:

F_436 â€“ account model and resolution
F_437 â€“ account lifecycle service
F_438 â€“ account management UI
F_439 â€“ account selection for actions and runs
F_440 â€“ account-aware execution
F_441 â€“ account-scoped provider sessions
F_442 â€“ account-scoped catalogs and runtime usage
F_443 â€“ account-scoped metrics and reset schedules



## Current state

* MDÂ² has one effective account per CLI. `AgentRunnerService`, model discovery, and account-usage polling copy the desktop process environment, so every Codex process uses the same Codex login and every Claude process uses the same Claude login.
* The existing global logins are the initial primary accounts:
  * Codex uses its normal `CODEX_HOME` (default `%USERPROFILE%\.codex`). File-based authentication is stored in `auth.json`; Codex can alternatively use the operating-system credential store.
  * Claude uses its normal `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (default `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`). On Windows, authentication is stored in `.credentials.json` in that directory.
* Codex supports a separate state directory through `CODEX_HOME`. Claude supports the same pattern through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Both variables select a complete CLI configuration directory, including credentials and other CLI state.
* Desktop agent selection stores `activeAgent`, one permission mode, and model, reasoning, and speed settings in `settingsByAgent`. There is no account collection or default account setting.
* Action definitions and run requests can override agent, model, reasoning, speed, and permission mode. Their schemas, editors, validation, history, and card-level remembered settings have no account field.
* A conversation stores provider sessions by `agent` only. Continuation and compaction therefore assume that every session for an agent belongs to the single global login.
* Model catalogs and Claude/Codex rate-limit snapshots are also keyed only by agent. Account-reset schedules and `usage_metrics.csv` cannot distinguish two accounts of the same provider.
* The config dialog has a specialized agent-profile editor, but there is no account-management service, directory picker, login bridge, or account editor.

## Implementation details

### Account model and desktop configuration

* Add a validated `desktop.agentAccounts` configuration value. Store accounts per supported built-in agent (`codex` and `claude`). Do not infer account support for custom agent profiles because MDÂ² does not know which configuration-directory variable they use.
* An account record contains:
  * `id`: stable identity used by selections, actions, runs, schedules, metrics, and conversations. Generate a UUID for extra accounts. Use stable reserved IDs for the two primary accounts.
  * `name`: editable display name. For an extra account, initialize it from the selected configuration folder name.
  * `kind`: `primary` or `directory`.
  * `configDirectory`: absolute directory path for a `directory` account only. The path is a persistence location and must never be used as account identity.
* Always resolve one primary account as the first account for Codex and one for Claude. A primary account has no configured directory: processes run with the normal inherited CLI environment and continue using the login already configured outside MDÂ². It can be renamed but cannot have its directory changed or be removed.
* Migrate existing desktop configuration by adding the two primary records and assigning the appropriate primary account to every existing `settingsByAgent` entry. This reflects hist

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

Introduce the shared account model used by the agent-account work in F_422. This task defines configuration and resolution only. It does not add account-management UI, login processes, or account-specific process environments.

## Current state

* Built-in Codex and Claude profiles use the desktop process environment and therefore each have one effective CLI login.
* `shared/agent_selection.mjs` stores model, thinking level, and speed settings per agent. It has no account setting.
* `desktop/src/shell/config.js` validates `desktop.agentSelection` and `desktop.agentProfiles`. The renderer mirrors those values through `config_entries.ts` and `config_service.ts`.
* Custom agent profiles do not declare which environment variable selects their provider configuration directory.

## Implementation details

* Add a validated `desktop.agentAccounts` configuration value for the supported built-in agents `codex` and `claude`. Do not infer account support for custom profiles.
* Each built-in agent always has an initial account representing the CLI login already available through the inherited environment. The initial account has a stable reserved ID, an editable name, kind `initial`, and no configured directory.
* Additional accounts have a generated UUID, an editable non-empty name, kind `directory`, and one resolved absolute `configDirectory`.
* Account IDs must be unique across the collection, account names must be unique within their agent, and normalized directory paths must be unique across directory accounts. Paths are persistence locations and never account identity.
* Treat a missing `desktop.agentAccounts` value as the two initial accounts without rewriting the stored desktop configuration. Saving account changes may persist the resolved collection normally.
* Add optional `accountId` support to `AgentSettings` and `FlatAgentSelection`. A missing account ID resolves to the selected built-in agent's initial account.
* Add shared account lookup, validation, and selection functions. An explicit unknown account, an account belonging to another agent, or an account selection on a custom profile is an error. Never replace an invalid explicit account with the initial account.
* Preserve account selection per agent when changing the active agent, following the existing `settingsByAgent` behavior.
* Do not migrate or backfill existing desktop settings. The missing-value rule is the compatibility behavior.
* Add focused shared, desktop-config, and renderer-config tests. Run the directly affected tests and lint in `app` and `desktop`.

## Acceptance criteria

* Codex and Claude each resolve an initial account when no account configuration or account ID is stored.
* Existing desktop configuration loads without being rewritten and keeps using the existing CLI login.
* Additional accounts use stable UUID identity; renaming an account or changing its directory does not change its ID.
* Explicit unknown, cross-agent, duplicate-ID, duplicate-name, and duplicate-directory values fail validation clearly.
* Custom agent profiles cannot receive an account selection.
* Selecting another agent restores that agent's remembered account selection.
* No credentials, CLI directories, conversations, schedules, activity files, or metrics are changed by this task.

Persist and project usage measurements and account-reset schedules separately for each agent account, using the account-scoped runtime snapshots from F_442.

## Current state

* `UsageMetricsService` writes account-usage and token-usage records to `usage_metrics.csv` without account identity.
* `ProjectUsageMetricsService` derives percentage deltas from baseline keys containing provider, limit, and window only.
* Account-reset triggers contain agent, limit, window, and expected reset time. `ActionSchedulerService` tracker keys and runtime subscriptions are agent-scoped.
* Existing CSV rows and schedule files predate account switching.

## Implementation details

* Add `account_id` to account-usage and token-usage CSV records and to renderer projections. New records always write the resolved account ID that produced the measurement.
* Accept the old CSV header when reading. A row without `account_id` belongs to that provider's initial account. Do not backfill old rows. New files use the expanded header; before the first account-aware append to an old file, extend its header while leaving its existing rows unchanged and continue treating their missing values as the initial account.
* Include account ID in account-usage baseline keys so percentage deltas are never calculated across accounts. Token-usage records use the account captured on the run by F_440.
* Add optional `accountId` to account-reset schedule triggers, draft state, validation, labels, persisted records, tracker observations, and tracker keys.
* A missing schedule account ID means the trigger agent's initial account. Do not rewrite existing schedule files merely because the field is absent.
* Build reset tracker options from account-scoped runtime snapshots. The schedule form selects an agent, then one of that agent's accounts, then a limit/window from the matching snapshot.
* Match reset observations and pending schedules by `(agent, accountId, limitId, windowId)`. A reset from one account must never fire a schedule registered for another account.
* Preserve the resolved account in the scheduled run selection so the eventual action does not follow a later desktop-default change.
* Removed or unavailable explicit accounts leave the schedule visible but invalid/unfireable with a clear account-specific error. Do not fall back to the initial account.
* Update stats/usage views and active-schedule labels where account identity is needed to distinguish otherwise identical rows or triggers.
* Add focused CSV parsing/writing, baseline, projection, schedule parsing, form, tracker, persistence, and scheduler tests.

## Acceptance criteria

* Account and token usage records identify the account that produced them.
* Percentage deltas and summaries never combine measurements from different accounts of the same provider.
* Existing CSV rows and schedules without account identity continue to represent the provider's initial account without data migration.
* Reset schedules select and display an account and fire only from that account's matching runtime observation.
* Changing the desktop default after schedule registration does not change the scheduled run's account.
* An explicit unavailable account blocks the affected schedule clearly and does not affect other accounts or schedules.
* Focused app and desktop tests and lint pass.

Found seven implementation problems. Tests were excluded as requested.

1. **High: Logged-out and non-isolated accounts can start runs.**  
   Run validation checks only directory existence and permissions. It does not check `loginRequired` or Codex `notIsolated` status. This can start an interactive or failing CLI process instead of producing the required account-specific error. See [agent_runner_service.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:244).  
   **Fix:** Reuse the desktop account-status check before every run, retry, resume, and compact. Require `available`; never fall back.

2. **High: Statistics still combine accounts.**  
   Actions are grouped by provider, not `(provider, accountId)`. Account-specific usage denominators are therefore compared with actions from every account of that provider. Totals also select one account series per provider and price all provider conversations with it. See [stats_usage_comparison_dataset.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/stats/stats_usage_comparison_dataset.ts:513) and [stats_totals_dataset.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/stats/stats_totals_dataset.ts:253).  
   **Fix:** Add `accountId` to stats action facts and group actions, tokens, rates, ratios, and costs by `(provider, accountId)`.

3. **High: Duplicate provider-session identities are accepted.**  
   Conversation parsing normalizes sessions but never rejects duplicate `(agent, resolved accountId)` entries. Resume then silently uses the first matching session, while updates leave the duplicate behind.
